title: The Shia telling
hook: Shia Muslims hold that the Prophet ﷺ had designated Ali, by God's command, as his successor

segments.voice: Yesterday: the Sunni telling, and the word khalifah. Your line was chosen by pledge. Today, the other telling, in its own words.

Go back into the small room beside the mosque. Ali ibn Abi Talib, the Prophet's cousin and the husband of his daughter Fatimah, is washing the body of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and preparing him for burial. He is not at the saqifah. In the Shia telling, it is while he is here that a leader is pledged to without him. For Shia Muslims, that scene carries the whole story. The question was not open, they hold. It had already been answered. Today's word: imam.
screen: `ALI IS WITH THE BODY.` → `NOT AT THE SAQIFAH.` → `ALREADY ANSWERED, THEY HOLD.`

segments.voice: In everyday Muslim life, the imam stands in front and leads the prayer. In Shia teaching it also names something larger: the rightful leader of the community after the Prophet, appointed by God, not elected by people. Shia Muslims hold that the Prophet designated Ali by God's command, and that Ali was the first imam. The word for that designation is nass, an explicit appointment. First, the Qur'an's account of Abraham. God tells him: I will make you an imam for the people. Abraham asks, and from my descendants? And God answers that His covenant does not reach the wrongdoers. Shia scholars read in this that leadership of this kind is God's to give. Second, a report that Sunni collections also carry, in Bukhari and Muslim. When the Prophet left Ali behind in Medina during an expedition, Ali was troubled, and the Prophet asked him: are you not content to be to me as Harun was to Musa, except that there is no prophet after me? Sunni scholars read that as love and trust on that occasion; Shia scholars, as a standing rank, a deputy and successor. And third, the hours we saw two days ago. Bukhari itself reports that Ali did not give his pledge to Abu Bakr for a time. For Shia Muslims, that says something. What both share matters too: Sunni and Shia Muslims both love and honor Ali. The disagreement is about what was given to him, and when. Tomorrow, words that both traditions report, spoken at a place called Ghadir Khumm.
screen: `IMAM: THE ONE WHO STANDS IN FRONT.` · `APPOINTED BY GOD, THEY HOLD.` · `AS HARUN WAS TO MUSA.` · `ALI HELD BACK HIS PLEDGE.` · then, large: `DESIGNATED, THEY SAY.`

segments.voice: If you grew up with the Sunni telling, let the Shia telling sit in you for a minute, in its own words, without answering it; if you grew up Shia, do the same with yesterday's. If neither is yours, pick any view you've never really listened to, and say it as its holders would, at its strongest, all the way to the end.
Imam. The one who stands in front to lead the prayer, and, in Shia teaching, the leader appointed by God after the Prophet, beginning with Ali. Today's word.
Your line: designated, they say. A telling, heard in its own words. Day eight hundred sixty-five, done.

howItsDone: Shia Muslims hold Ali ibn Abi Talib to be the first imam after the Prophet, designated by God, and remember the imams of the Prophet's family in prayers, visits and commemorations.
